chunks: Al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was asked about a mukātab who was unable to fulfill his manumission contract, though he had already paid part of it. He said:
It should be paid on his behalf from the funds of charity.
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in His Book: 'and for freeing slaves.'

key_terms.الرِّقَابِ: the category of slaves or captives to be freed
key_terms.مَالِ الصَّدَقَةِ: charity funds, meaning wealth allocated for prescribed charitable disbursement
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a contractual agreement to purchase his freedom
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: his manumission contract and its required payments
key_terms.يُؤَدَّى: the payment is to be fulfilled or discharged

ai.seo_question: Can zakat or charity funds be used to help a mukatab complete his emancipation contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a mukātab who cannot complete his contracted payments may be assisted from charity funds. It cites the Qur'anic category 'and for freeing slaves' as proof that zakat resources may be used to help secure emancipation.
